questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Weather/climate, safety, and cultural environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not much information was given upon my arrival (or at all). My best tip is to check your KU email frequently and communicate with the other Danish exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Make sure to visit campus before the semester starts, to figure out where your classes will be taking place.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Start looking for accommodation early. I recommend HousingAnywhere, which is the platform I found my apartment on, but I know of others who found housing through SpotAHome.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Milan offers great public transportation, but I would recommend to live within the city circle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The regisration process is quite old school, but easy to figure out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the classes I wanted as there is no maximum of students per class. However, some classes overlap, so make sure to check the schedule for each course before you register.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My best tip is to try out different classes before you register your courses. It's also possible to change courses throughout the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is lower than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: (Almost) no required readings and minimum group and homework. However, attendance was taken, so you have to show up for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Smart cities, Artificial Intelligence and digital transformation law, Comparative Labour Law, Competition Law and Economics, Access to Justice in A Multilevel Constitutional System, and Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend Competition Law and Economics. The professor is great, and I actually learned something during class, unlike many of my other courses. I can also recommend Smart Cities if you want an easy exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is just as expensive, if not more expensive, than in Copenhagen. Groceries were also quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Though I didn't personally made use of it, there is the ESN Milano Statale group which plan activities, trips, night outs, city tours, and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of Milan's rich cultural scene. I highly recommend visiting Pinacoteca di Brera. Also, China Town, though small, offers great food for cheap prices.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Milan is close to a load of other great cities, so I recommend taking advantage of this by going on day trips. For instance, Lake Como is just one hour away by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn some Italian.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Regarding school, everything is very "unplanned" and us students are poorly informed. I never really knew what was expected of me at the exams, nor what the exams consisted of exactly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Other than the food and Aperitivo - The easy-going and relaxed vibe (except when it comes to school).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Save up some money so you can experience what Milan has to offer. 2) Don't worry too much about the lack of information - everything will work out in the end! 3) Don't stress about not doing something new every day. There is a lot of different ways to enjoy your exchange, and a big part of it is also "just" living a normal, student life in a new city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to apply for the codice fiscale before you leave Denmark. It's much, much easier than having to obtain it once you have landed in Italy (I'm speaking from experience).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and being able to spend my weekends traveling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my codice fiscale, making sure my courses didn't overlap, and not being properly informed about how/when my exams would take place.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
